title: Speed up golden tests (10-15min → 1-4min) starting with instrumentation
description:
Golden tests take 10-15 minutes in CI. Other CI actions take 1-4 minutes. We want goldens in that range too.

Prior attempts:
- Maven caching (may not have been set up correctly — worth revisiting)
- Persistent JVMs for bridges (not spinning up new ones per test)
- Not loading all Magic sets

Since the obvious wins haven't helped, step 1 is instrumentation: figure out exactly where the time is going before trying more fixes.

Work items:

1. **Add detailed timing instrumentation** to the golden test pipeline. Break down wall-clock time into: JVM startup, server startup, bridge connection, game setup, per-turn execution, export/comparison, teardown. Log per-test and aggregate timing. The goal is a clear flamegraph-style picture of where the 10-15 minutes goes.

2. **Expose golden run stats on /internals.** We run goldens far more often than real LLM games, so golden timing data is plentiful. Show trends: total suite time, per-test time, breakdown by phase. This ties into the internals page (issues/internals-page.json).

3. **Optimize based on what the instrumentation reveals.** Don't guess — let the data point to the bottleneck. Possible areas (speculative until instrumented): server startup per test, game state initialization, set loading that's still happening despite the fix, sequential test execution that could be parallelized, export/comparison overhead.
